Basic ATC

Informe establecido

An instruction for the pilot to inform ATC when the aircraft is established on a specified segment of the approach, typically the localizer or final approach course.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Informe establecido?

In this glossary, Informe establecido refers to: An instruction for the pilot to inform ATC when the aircraft is established on a specified segment of the approach, typically the localizer or final approach course.

How is Informe establecido used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Big Jet 345, gire a la derecha rumbo 240, descienda a 3000 pies, informe establecido en el localizador pista 27 derecha."

Why does Informe establecido matter in aviation?

Informe establecido matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Informe establecido?

Informe establecido is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

An instruction for the pilot to inform ATC when the aircraft is established on a specified segment of the approach, typically the localizer or final approach course.

Operational example

Big Jet 345, turn right heading 240, descend to 3000 feet, report established localizer runway 27 Right.

Localized term

Informe establecido

Localized example

Big Jet 345, gire a la derecha rumbo 240, descienda a 3000 pies, informe establecido en el localizador pista 27 derecha.
